baseline: The previously derived policy-cost area model and the original P1 execution cycles. All original results remain unchanged.
configuration: Two equal-sized configuration regions, each sized for the largest segment of this workload; both share original dual-port SRAM macros. This is a proposed implementation, not the archived RTL.

area.scope: Selected accelerator components, identical scope to policy-cost. Values are library area units, not independently verified mm^2.
rules: Reduce only native command/patch SRAM and CGRA packet SRAM banks using existing macro depth/width and integer rounding.
Retain core SRAM, SPM, compute, adapters and original control logic from the prior policy-specific model.
Two configuration regions share a dual-port macro address space; they are not separately padded physical SRAM banks.
Profile slots decrease but existing minimum macro depths save no depth bank. Keep the already policy-adjusted word width.
Do not scale total hardware area by the number of live configurations.
New buffer ownership, address remapping and concurrent configuration/replay logic are not synthesized or separately priced. Retained logic does not prove these functions fit.

capacity.ResNet: Native6n; CGRA4 per IP; profiles2. For n=4 this holds all H configurations.
capacity.GPT2: Native32; CGRA24 per IP; profiles16, twice peaks16/12/8 verified by archived host plan.
capacity.GCN: Two segments already fill the complete existing H cache; no additional capacity saving.

performance.main_boundary: Execution-focused, initial segment prepared before timing. Later required refills are counted. Where two buffers retain the complete graph, reuse them across repetitions without gratuitous reloads.
performance.symbols: T=original H total, E=original H execute, O=T-E, C=measured original full capture, K=segments.
performance.resnet_point: T+(K-1)*max(0,(C-E)/K), assuming equal configuration/execution cost per segment. Initial C/K is outside timing. Applies n=1,2; n=4 retains whole schedule.
performance.resnet_sensitivity: O+max(E,C*(K-1)/K) through T+C*(K-1)/K, under the stated unchanged-work and overlap assumptions.
performance.gpt_sensitivity: T through T+ceil(C*36/32). 36 job reloads vs32 unique jobs; packets3293 vs2999 per IP. Native commands and profiles do not duplicate. Inflating all C by36/32 is a deliberately loose linear-cost scenario; no segment timestamps support a point estimate.
performance.full_reload_columns: Separate sensitivity columns include all configuration loading: O+max(E,C_model) through T+C_model. Do not compare these to original setup-excluded policies as if boundaries were equal.
assumptions: Same configuration write throughput as old capture.
No added CPU/MMIO/interconnect contention or buffer-switch overhead.
Two-region refill requires RTL support; not validated in archived hardware.
The recorded execution interval includes launch/synchronization, so treating it as available overlap time is optimistic.
performance.limitations: No per-segment cycle trace, new simulation or timing closure. These are conditional model/sensitivity values, not confidence intervals or guaranteed physical upper/lower bounds. Original synthesis capacity/SRAM adaptations differ from simulated hardware and the original component synthesis did not close the10ns target.

validation: 40 data consistency checks passed: nine H settings,27 unique comparisons, SRAM integer counts and deduction sums, interval ordering, unchanged Manual/Auto rows, source hashes.
Independent timing arithmetic and measurement-boundary review passed.
GPT per-segment resources extracted using archived host harness for1/2/4C.

files.hybrid.csv: Nine H area and timing estimates with baseline, capacities and timing boundaries.
files.comparison27.csv: All27 policy/configuration rows with modeled AE and speedup sensitivity. Manual/Auto retain prior derived area and original cycles.
files.memory.csv: Every additional SRAM bank deduction, source layer and macro count.
files.evidence: Archived timing extraction and host-plan outputs.
